This is a classic presentation for an IDH-mutant glioma, as IDH-wildtype tumors in adults are typically glioblastomas which almost invariably enhance. overall_comment: The imaging findings for this 44-year-old patient are highly characteristic of a lower-grade, IDH-mutant glioma, given the complete lack of enhancement and insular location. The combination of IDH-mutant and 1p/19q non-codeleted status defines an astrocytoma, and the absence of high-grade features supports a WHO grade 2 classification. The primary source of diagnostic uncertainty is the absence of the T2-FLAIR mismatch sign, which slightly lowers the confidence in the astrocytoma (non-codeleted) subtype prediction.
